summary:
Florida stands under the United States national framework and adds a state layer a trans visitor meets directly on the ground, most sharply in public facilities. Under the Facility Requirements Based on Sex Act (Fla. Stat. 553.865), in force since 1 July 2023, a trans person may not use a restroom or changing facility consistent with their gender identity in buildings owned or leased by state or local government: state offices, courthouses, legislative offices, prisons and jails, local immigration detention facilities, state parks, toll-road plazas, airports, convention centres, stadiums, state universities and school campuses. The statute purports to reach all schools, public and private. Refusing to leave after an authority figure orders departure can be charged as criminal trespass. Private businesses fall outside its scope, and the ACLU advises fact-specific judgement and legal counsel in borderline settings.

The law has been enforced once in this record. Marcy Rheintgen, a 20-year-old trans college student, was arrested on 19 March 2025 at the Florida State Capitol after police, alerted in advance, took her into custody while she was washing her hands in a women's restroom; she had declared "I am here to break the law." She was charged with misdemeanour trespass carrying up to 60 days in jail, in what is believed to be the first arrest under Florida's transgender bathroom restrictions. On 20 June 2025 Leon County Judge Lashawn Riggans threw the case out: as a defendant charged under the statute she had no standing to argue that the law itself was illegitimate, so the prohibition was never substantively tested in court.

The Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the underlying restriction in January 2023, reversing its own August 2020 ruling that a Ponte Vedra Beach high school had violated the law by refusing a transgender student consistent restroom use, and the restriction was codified on 17 May 2023.

State identity documents diverge from what a trans visitor may hold. In January 2024 the Department of Highway Services and Motor Vehicles banned issuing any driver's licence bearing a gender marker different from sex assigned at birth, and treats holders, users and applicants as criminally guilty of fraud, with suspension and revocation of the licence. In July 2024 transgender people born in Florida could not update or change the sex on their birth certificates despite legislation that expressly permitted it. Before that closure, an amended birth certificate required an application, a notarised affidavit and a physician letter confirming appropriate clinical treatment for gender transition without requiring surgery or sterilisation; after 2011 a licence name change required a court order alongside a physician statement.

Gender-affirming care is restricted in state law. After an August 2022 rule change citing state guidance against such care, the Medical Board required on 31 October 2022 a 24-hour waiting period for adults before sexual reassignment surgery, and on 4 November 2022 approved a ban on gender-affirming healthcare for minors that took effect 16 March 2023 and was codified 17 May 2023. Minors under 18 cannot receive puberty blockers, hormone therapy or confirming surgeries unless intersex, and a board memo stated that social transition should not be a treatment option. The same codification created adult barriers, including a ban on insurance coverage for the care and a requirement that a physician rather than a nurse practitioner administer it. Senate Bill 254's Physicians Only provision prohibited nurse practitioners and physician assistants from providing gender-affirming care to transgender adults, which the Human Rights Campaign reported disrupted care for an estimated 80 percent or more of transgender clinic patients, with temporary or permanent suspensions after signing.

The care bans have been litigated. Three plaintiffs obtained a preliminary injunction on 6 June 2024 limited to themselves, that injunction was stayed on 26 August 2024 by the Eleventh Circuit, and a federal judge permanently blocked the provisions banning care for minors and adults in June 2024. The record documents no later appellate resolution of that ruling.

A May 2023 law allows medical practitioners to decline treatment on grounds of conscience, religion or belief, effective immediately by emergency clause; critics argued it permits refusal of gender-affirming care as well as PrEP and abortion access. A separate May 2023 law banning adult live performances anywhere a minor might view them was preliminarily enjoined on 23 June 2023 as not all drag performance is obscene.

State protection on gender identity is thin. Florida statutes do not address gender identity discrimination in employment, housing or other areas, and nursing home and hospital protections in place since 2000, amended in 2007, cover sexual orientation but not gender identity. The state hate-crime law provides harsher penalties for crimes motivated by sexual orientation but does not cover gender identity. Counties and cities comprising about 55 percent of the population, among them Jacksonville, Miami, Tampa, Orlando, St Petersburg, Tallahassee and West Palm Beach, do prohibit discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in private and public employment, housing and public accommodations. In February 2021 the Florida Commission on Human Relations announced it would enforce Bostock v. Clayton County (15 June 2020) across employment, housing and public accommodations, and Glenn v. Brumby (December 2011) held that employment discrimination based on transgender status is sex discrimination.

Equality Florida took what it called the unprecedented step of issuing a travel advisory on 12 April 2023, warning of risks to the health, safety and freedom of people considering short or long-term travel or relocation to Florida, citing laws hostile to LGBTQ people alongside reproductive-health restrictions, gun-safety rollbacks and book bans and curriculum censorship. The advisory followed a wave of visitor safety enquiries; the organisation reports events and conferences cancelling. The Human Rights Campaign joined the advisory in May 2023, citing legislation signed by Governor DeSantis, while stopping short of a boycott.
tangentialFactors:
Florida's bathroom restriction is part of a wider pattern rather than an isolated statute: at least 14 states have adopted laws barring trans women from women's bathrooms at schools and some government buildings. The 2025 Rheintgen arrest is described in the source as believed to be the first arrest under Florida's transgender bathroom restrictions, so the enforcement record in this jurisdiction rests on a single documented case.

Municipal conversion-therapy bans, concentrated in the Miami metropolitan area, have been struck down by the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, removing a local protection that some cities had adopted. In September 2023 Lake Worth Beach became an official LGBTQ sanctuary city, pledging to protect and defend LGBTQ rights.

Florida's exclusion of transgender girls and women from female school sports dates from 1 June 2021, predating the 2023 facility law by two years, and the state Attorney General has pursued competitions, including an Irish step dancing competition and Miss America, on the grounds that allowing transgender competitors is deceptive and deprives women of fair competition.

Same-sex marriage has been legal in Florida since 6 January 2015, when Brenner v. Scott (21 August 2014) held the state's ban unconstitutional under the Fourteenth Amendment, superseding the 1977 statutory ban and the November 2008 Amendment 2 prohibition. Nine counties, thirty cities and one town offer domestic partnership benefits.
localsOnly:
Resident-facing restrictions extend well beyond visitor facilities. On 23 August 2023 the Board of Education approved firing employees of 28 public community and state colleges who enter a forbidden bathroom, and on 18 October 2023 it voted to apply a similar restriction to private college and university buildings including student housing, with compliance proof required by 1 April 2024.

Senate Bill 254, effective 17 May 2023, permits child custody modification on the basis that a child received or might receive gender-affirming care, and legislation of April 2023 allows a court to modify or nullify an out-of-state parental custody agreement if the child is allowed or threatened with access to such care. Opponents described the provisions as permitting removal of children across state lines; protests saw trans children detained and one arrested for disturbing the peace.

On 23 April 2026 the legislature passed HB 1001/SB 1134, effective January 2027, prohibiting state and local funding for or promotion of diversity, equity and inclusion as defined to include gender identity, enforceable through lawsuits and removal of officials. It has been interpreted as barring government support to LGBTQ organisations and events; Palm Beach County denied a HUD grant to repair the air conditioning at the headquarters of Compass, an LGBTQ community centre.

In early 2023 the Florida High School Athletics Association recommended that female athletes supply menstrual cycle information to a school-accessible database, a measure speculated to serve enforcement of abortion restrictions and detection of trans women.

Local ordinances are the practical route to protection: counties and cities covering about 55 percent of Florida's population prohibit discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment, housing and public accommodations, while state statute does not. Conversion-therapy bans adopted by a number of cities, mainly in the Miami metropolitan area, were struck down by the Eleventh Circuit.
outOfScopeNotes:
The 2023 facility statute has not been substantively tested in court. The only prosecution documented here was dismissed on 20 June 2025 because the defendant lacked standing to challenge the law's validity, so the scope and application of Fla. Stat. 553.865 remain unresolved on the merits.

The appellate status of the gender-affirming care rulings is unresolved in this record: a preliminary injunction of 6 June 2024 was limited to three plaintiffs, the Eleventh Circuit stayed it on 26 August 2024, and a federal judge permanently blocked the care bans in June 2024, with no later appellate outcome documented.

Whether the January 2024 driver's licence fraud rule or the July 2024 birth-certificate closure has been challenged in court is not sourced here, nor is any figure for how many licences or certificates have been affected.

The enforcement frequency of the facility law beyond the single March 2025 arrest is not sourced; no count of warnings, trespass charges or removals under the statute appears in the inventory.

A January 2022 report of Florida's first sex-unknown birth certificate is recorded without explanation of the category or its subsequent treatment, and whether that option remains available is unresolved.

Whether HB 1001/SB 1134, effective January 2027, has drawn litigation before its effective date is not sourced.
